source.title: Combating Label Noise in Deep Learning Using Abstention
source.authors: S. Thulasidasan; Tanmoy Bhattacharya; Jeff A. Bilmes; Gopinath Chennupati; J. Mohd-Yusof

record.file_problem: none; full paper text including appendices is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study examines learning patterns before memorization during training, but uses a deep abstaining classifier and structured label noise rather than the original standard-network setup.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. (2016) and Arpit et al. (2017) for prior findings about random-label memorization; those cited results are not this study's rows. Its own Table 1 reports downstream classification accuracy after filtering noisy samples, not training error on the corrupted set, so those values do not test V1 or V4. Figure 4 reports fixed-alpha abstention and validation behavior during the smudging experiment.
record.test_reason: Section 5 reports the study's own training trajectories and explicitly interprets them as learning patterns before memorizing randomized labels, bearing on V6 through an abstention-based method.
record.authors_conclusion: The recorded memorization conclusion accurately summarizes Section 5: the DAC learns patterns first, but abstention does not generally prevent eventual memorization with sufficiently long training and a small learning rate. The paper's broader conclusion is that DAC abstention learns structured-noise features and helps clean noisy datasets for downstream classification.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an abstention loss and structured label corruption on smudged images, rather than the original standard-network random-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: For fixed-alpha runs, abstention drops steeply at epochs 60 and 120, coinciding with learning-rate decay; the authors report generalization also suffers after memorization begins.

fits_no_version.finding: Baseline DNN test accuracy exceeds 82% on non-corrupted data and falls below 75% in the smudging experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The structured-smudging and partial-label-randomization setting reduces baseline classification accuracy.

record.problems: The learning-order result is reported for a DAC with an abstention loss and structured smudging, not a standard network trained on completely random labels. Figure 4 values are not numerically reported in the text, and uncertainty estimates are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 and Appendix C report downstream test accuracy after DAC filtering and retraining, so these values do not measure the claimed original-model training fit or test error. Figures 1 and 2 report abstention and risk-coverage behavior for structured-noise scenarios, not the learning-order outcome in V6.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit together with steadily increasing test error across corruption fractions from zero to complete randomization.
Effects of adding or removing weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning order in standard non-abstaining networks and under unstructured label randomization; direct, separate measurements of fitting clean and randomized labels over training.

missing.what: A learning-order row for automatically tuned alpha: initial learning, abstention stabilizing near 10% during epochs 120–150, and reported entry into memorization after learning-rate reduction at epoch 160. The record's exclusion of Figure 1 overlooks this relevant accompanying text.
missing.locator: Section 3.2, Results; Figure 1b; Section 5 final paragraph

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for the versions. Its modified loss encourages abstention rather than memorization, so eventual memorization is not a behavior directly imposed by its objective. No numerical training-error result establishes V1 or V4.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether standard networks fit a completely random labeling with near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
No comparison of training time for fitting true versus random labels is reported.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input fitting experiment is reported.
The study does not measure perfect training fit and test error across a sweep from clean to completely random labels.
The study does not test whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent random-label fitting, or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.

The study tests learning order only in its DAC structured-smudging experiment with fixed abstention penalties; it does not establish the claim for standard networks generally or for arbitrary random labels.

rows.subject: VGG-16 DAC
rows.operation_detail: Trained with fixed abstention penalty on a dataset where labels of smudged training images were randomized; tracked abstention and validation behavior over training.

conditions.value: 10% of training images smudged and labels randomized
fixed; multiple values indicated by color

rows.measure: Abstention behavior and validation generalization over epochs as indicators of transition to memorizing randomized labels.
rows.value: The authors report that abstention on the smudged samples did not persist indefinitely; steep abstention reductions occurred at epochs 60 and 120, and generalization suffered once the memorization phase began.
rows.note: The text explicitly says the DAC first learns patterns before descending into memorization. Figure 4 varies fixed alpha; separate numeric values are not provided in the text.
rows.check: The learning-order conclusion is stated in Section 5, not solely in the figure. Abstention reductions and declining validation accuracy provide indirect evidence; separate training-fit curves for clean and randomized labels are not reported. Restrict the finding to runs that learn and subsequently lose abstention: sufficiently small fixed alpha can instead produce complete abstention and prevent further learning.

source_check.locator_found: Sections 3.1–3.2 establish the setup; Section 5 and Figure 4 describe fixed-alpha abstention, validation performance, and learning order.

rows.subject: Baseline DNN softmax
rows.operation_detail: Trained with standard K-class cross-entropy on clean data and on data with randomized labels for smudged images; compared test accuracy at full coverage.

conditions.value: 10% of training images smudged and labels randomized

rows.value: under 75% on the label-randomized smudged set
rows.note: This is a result on structured partial label corruption and test accuracy; it does not establish the claim versions' complete-random-label fitting or training-error conditions.
rows.check: The reported accuracies are correct, but test-accuracy degradation at one corruption fraction does not establish any version's training-fit or learning-order requirements. The test set also contains 10% smudged images, so the comparison does not isolate training-label corruption.

relationships.condition: VGG-16 DAC on STL-10 with 10% smudged, label-randomized training images; fixed-alpha runs that proceed into memorization
relationships.reason: R1: Section 5 explicitly reports patterns learned before memorization; abstention falls at learning-rate reductions around epochs 60 and 120, accompanied by worse validation generalization. Evidence for memorization is indirect.
relationships.display_finding: Patterns were learned first, while abstention fell around learning-rate reductions at epochs 60 and 120 alongside worse validation generalization.
